key_insight: LLM agents can translate household preferences into reliable multi-appliance energy schedules, achieving near-MILP performance when connected to live tools and native function calling.
engineering_relevance: This work shows a practical path for embedding natural-language control into home energy management systems to reduce electricity costs and improve demand-response automation.
method: Built a tool-calling ReAct agent using live Octopus Agile prices, weather forecasts, photovoltaic estimates, household usage data, and a retrieval-augmented knowledge base.
Benchmarked GPT-4o-mini, Gemini 2.5 Flash, and Claude Sonnet 4.6 against a MILP ground truth across tariff days, constraint conflicts, and weather-aware solar co-optimization.
Compared native function calling with text-parsed action interfaces, then tested week-long deployment savings against an oracle and off-peak baseline.
evidence_signal: Across scenarios, native function calling achieved 100% scheduling success and agents captured 96.7–98.0% of oracle savings over a simulated week, with projected annual savings of about GBP 1,270 versus an off-peak timer baseline.
watch_item: Performance drops sharply when actions are text-parsed instead of function-called, so robust tool interfaces and constraint handling are essential for real deployments.
paper_title: LLMs for Agentic Home Energy Management
